issues.failure_explanation: The sample squared correlation between \(\hat r\) and \(\psi\) uses the residual sample variance \(\frac1n\sum(\hat r_i-\bar{\hat r})^2\) in the denominator. The displayed \(e_n\) uses \(\frac1n\sum\hat r_i^2\), so it equals the squared correlation only when \(\bar{\hat r}=0\). Diagnostic residuals are not guaranteed to have zero sample mean, especially on an independent diagnostic set.

failure_location.quote: is the squared residual--probe correlation, i.e.\ the fraction of residual variance that a linear correction along \(\psi\) would remove

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \(\hat\sigma_r^2\) in the effect-size denominator by the sample variance of the diagnostic residuals, or state and enforce that diagnostic residuals are centered.
issues.overall_effect: The reported effect sizes and the interpretation of the tolerance \(\varepsilon\) as a fraction of residual variance are unreliable when diagnostic residual means are nonzero.
issues.title: Effect size is not squared correlation when diagnostic residuals have nonzero mean
issues.why_classification: A local correction to the denominator restores the intended interpretation; the diagnostic concept and main conclusions survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: no out-of-basis direction removes more than \(\varepsilon\) of the residual variance

issues.failure_explanation: The condition \(\max_\psi e_n(\psi)\le\varepsilon\) bounds only the squared correlation of each individual probe. The orthogonality condition requires the residual to have zero projection onto the entire out-of-basis subspace. A residual that is a sum of many small components across an orthonormal basis can have total out-of-basis projection larger than \(\varepsilon\) while every individual \(e_n(\psi)\) is \(\le\varepsilon\). Thus the stop rule can falsely certify the barrier.

failure_location.quote: declare the barrier reached when no out-of-basis probe is both significant \emph{and} practically large---operationally, when \(\max_\psi e_n(\psi)\le\varepsilon\) for a task-set tolerance \(\varepsilon\) fixed independently of \(n\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the max individual probe effect size with the fraction of residual variance explained by the full out-of-basis probe span, for example by regressing the residual on all out-of-basis probes and using the resulting \(R^2\), or otherwise test the joint subspace.
issues.overall_effect: The procedure may declare the conditional-mean barrier reached even when substantial reducible structure is distributed across many out-of-basis directions, leading to an overestimate of the aleatoric floor.
issues.title: Stop rule uses max individual probe effect size, not joint out-of-basis projection
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial change to the diagnostic statistic is needed; the overall diagnostic approach can survive, so it is not a total loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition and the claimed range \([0,1]\) require \(\Var(Y)>0\). When \(Y\) is almost surely constant, \(\Var(Y)=0\) and \(R^2\) is undefined. The source does not state this nondegeneracy condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume \(\Var(Y)>0\) throughout the discussion of \(R^2\), or handle the constant case separately.
issues.overall_effect: The coefficient of determination and the explained-variance ceiling are not defined in the degenerate constant-output case.
issues.title: R² undefined when Var(Y)=0
issues.why_classification: A standard local nondegeneracy condition fixes the issue without affecting the main results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Because the \(K=8\) stencils in a snapshot are spatially correlated, raw per-row significance would be overstated; we therefore form a snapshot-clustered statistic

issues.failure_explanation: The statistic \(e_n\) is computed from sample averages over the spatially correlated stencil-closure pairs. Spatial correlation affects the sampling distribution and expectation of these averages through covariance terms; it is not eliminated by taking a ratio. The point estimate is a sample moment, but its uncertainty and bias are not unaffected by the correlation.

failure_location.quote: Because \(e_n\) is a ratio of second moments, it is unaffected by spatial correlation among the \(K\) stencils recorded at one time step, so it can be read directly.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a spatially clustered or effective-sample-size version of the effect-size statistic, or explicitly account for spatial correlation in its uncertainty.
issues.overall_effect: The L96 effect-size diagnostic is presented without accounting for spatial correlation, so the reported effect sizes and the stop-rule comparison to \(\varepsilon\) may be less reliable than claimed.
issues.title: Effect size claimed unaffected by spatial correlation
issues.why_classification: A local statistical correction is needed for the L96 diagnostic; the main mathematical results are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: After a burn-in period, the trajectory is downsampled to reduce short-time correlation and then split into time blocks.

issues.failure_explanation: The one-sample t-statistic assumes the snapshot moments \(H_t\) are independent. The diagnostic snapshots are consecutive time samples from a dynamical system; downsampling only reduces, and does not eliminate, temporal autocorrelation. The usual standard error \(\hat s_H/\sqrt{60}\) is therefore biased, invalidating the reported t-statistics and threshold.

failure_location.quote: we therefore form a snapshot-clustered statistic, averaging the row product \(r_{t,k}\psi(S_{t,k})\) within each snapshot to a snapshot moment \(H_t = K^{-1}\sum_k r_{t,k}\psi(S_{t,k})\) and computing the one-sample \(t\)-statistic \(t_{59}(\psi)=\sqrt{60}\,\bar H/\hat s_H\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a HAC/block bootstrap or other autocorrelation-robust standard error for the snapshot moments.
issues.overall_effect: The significance check corroborating the L96 closure selection is not statistically valid as reported.
issues.title: Snapshot t-test ignores temporal correlation
issues.why_classification: The significance test is supporting rather than primary; a local correction to the standard error suffices.
